To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the reaction between the A(n) B(n-1) O(3n) perovskite oxide phases and LiH proceeds by reductive lithiation, leading to the insertion of lithium cations into the B-cation deficient perovkite framework.

the reaction of the A(n) B(n-1) O(3n) phases with LiH results in the formation of new A(n) Bn O(3n+1) phases, where the A(n) and B(n-1 ) cations are replaced by the A(n) Li and Bn cations respectively.
reductive lithium insertion into B-deficient niobium peroxkite oxides proceeds by lithium intercalation, leading to a range of novel materials with interesting properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, structure and lithium intercalation chemistry of the cation deficient niobate perovskite materials Ba(5)TiNb(3)NbO(15) Ba(6)LaTiNb(4),O(18) Ba(6)LiTinb(4),O (18) and Ba,LaNb(3),O (12).
the synthesis and characterisation of a series of new lithium containing oxides, and the investigation of their properties.
the synthesis of a range of cation deficient perosvkite oxides, their reaction with LiH to form lithium intercalated derivatives and their characterisation by a range of experimental methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cation ordering in these phases, which is a consequence of the cation vacancies, is maintained during the insertion process.

the reaction of LiH with A(n)B (n-1)O (3n) cations deficient perovskites leads to reductive lithium insertion into the B-site, which in the cases where the cation ordering is retained in the lithiated product, leads to the formation of a Li-Nb or Ti-Li-Nb ordered perovskite.

the reaction between LiH and A(n)B(m)O(3m) phases proceeds by reductive Li insertion and the resulting phases are cation ordered, with the cation ordering of the parent phase being faithfully retained, with the exception of Ba(3)Nb(2)O(9) which forms Ba(3)LiNb(2)TiO(9) with no cation ordering.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the B-cation deficient perovkite oxides can be used as a host for the insertion of lithium and other alkali metal cations, leading to the synthesis of a variety of new phases.
lithium insertion into the cation deficient peroxskite oxides proceeds by reductive insertion of the lithium, with the lithium cations displcing the cation vacancies.
the cation deficient peroxskite oxides are able to accommodate lithium by a combination of cation ordering and reductive insertion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
reductive lithium insertion into B-deficient perovskite oxide phases can lead to the formation of novel lithium insertion materials, with interesting properties.
reductive lithium insertion into cation deficient niobate perovskite materials is an effective way of stabilizing lithium cations in the B-site of perovskite structures.
the reactivity of the A(n) B(n-1) O(3n) phases towards LiH is determined by the cation order in these phases, which is in turn a function of the B/B ratio.
